# Alera patches

This directory is a local, checked-in fork of `desktop_updater` 2.7.0 from `https://github.com/MarlonJD/flutter_desktop_updater`, tag `v2.7.0`. The verified tag object is `0f1e72140d461f9eae3192ade47112229a24de29` and resolves to commit `bc5012233b2e4428215579e57b8245dd18f3256b`. The upstream package is distributed under the MIT license; the original `LICENSE` file remains unchanged.

The fork keeps the package's public release metadata, signature verification, safe path and symlink checks, platform staging, and native installation handoff. Alera only changes the runtime staging boundary: ZIP decoding and file writes run in a cancellable worker isolate, whose filesystem mutations and stream closes complete synchronously before acknowledgement; the parent waits for isolate exit before cleanup. Streamed archive input and output avoid loading the complete ZIP into the main isolate, while decoder memory can still scale with compressed entries inside the worker. The public download API accepts injected operation and cleanup process runners, a file-mode applier, and a cancellation token.

The application supplies the file-mode applier from its syscall-backed POSIX mode boundary. The package's standalone `defaultFileModeApplier` remains available for consumers that do not inject an application boundary. Release CLI process helpers are outside the Flutter runtime staging path and retain their upstream behavior.

The app must call `DesktopUpdater.downloadZipFirstUpdate` with `runProcess`, `runCleanupProcess`, `applyFileMode`, and `cancellationToken` from its updater-owned boundaries. The package's default `ProcessRunner` remains a compatibility fallback without token access, so it cannot cancel an active child; Alera supplies the token-aware operation runner and the independent cleanup runner. The cleanup runner remains usable after cancellation so mounted DMG volumes are detached. It must not import `desktop_updater/src` paths.

When no custom macOS distribution verifier is supplied, `runProcess` is threaded into DMG and PKG verification, mounting, and copy commands, while `runCleanupProcess` is used for DMG detach. UpdateClient supplies an owned staging mountpoint, allowing a canceled attach to be detached even if it fails before returning parsed metadata; a failed normal detach retries with `-force` only for that owned mountpoint. The extractor rejects pre-existing symlink roots and path ancestors before creating or replacing staged files. macOS `.app` internal symlinks remain handled by the signed `ditto` path.

The package-local repository contract tests read selected documentation and CI fixtures that are omitted from the hosted package archive. Those files were copied unchanged from the verified `v2.7.0` source tag, including the workflow, harness and execution-plan documents, release documentation, and `.gitignore`; no generated cache, lockfile, or external checkout is included.

PKG metadata expansion and residual staging-directory scans retain the upstream cooperative boundary; their native commands use the injected operation runner, while DMG detach uses the independent cleanup runner. A future API revision can thread the cancellation token through PKG parsing without widening this fork's public contract today. The staging catch logs secondary cleanup failures through `dart:developer` and rethrows the original error with its original stack, so cleanup diagnostics cannot replace cancellation, hash, or process failures.
